mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions 'the difference between the number of X and Y', interpret it as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order as written.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase 'difference between the number of X and Y' appears, either alone or within a larger equation.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between A and B' as |A - B| or as just A, ignoring B.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form 'A has N more than B' (including combined forms) into the equation A = B + N (or equivalently B = A - N).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly gives a numeric difference between two persons.
mathgap.example: Reading 'A has 5 more than B' as A = B - 5 or ignoring the sign.

mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When processing a transfer statement, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, updating their current counts before any later statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form 'X gives N items to Y' appears.
mathgap.example: Delaying the transfer until after later equations, causing those equations to use outdated counts.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When encountering a direct count statement, set the person's count to the given number at that point, but allow later transfers to modify it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement like 'X has N items' appears.
mathgap.example: Treating a direct count as immutable and ignoring later transfers that change the count.

mathgap.title: Preserve Difference Order
mathgap.principle: When equating a 'has more than' difference to a 'difference between' two persons, preserve the order of terms on both sides as written.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a relational statement equates two difference expressions.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'difference between A and B' as B - A, swapping the order.

mathgap.title: Temporal Evaluation of Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: When evaluating a relational statement, use the current counts of the persons at that point in the text, after any prior transfers or updates.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a relational statement appears after earlier statements that modify counts.
mathgap.example: Using a person's pre‑transfer count in an equation that occurs after the transfer.

mathgap.title: Combined Sum Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement gives a combined total for several persons, interpret it as the sum of those persons' counts equals the given total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement mentions a total for a group of people.
mathgap.example: Treating 'A, B, and C have a total of 30' as only A having 30.

mathgap.title: Split Equally Among Recipients (Additive)
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all their items equally among recipients, set the donor's count to 0 and add the appropriate share to each recipient.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among others.
mathgap.example: Leaving the donor's count unchanged after splitting.

mathgap.title: Difference Cancellation
mathgap.principle: If an equation equates two differences that share a common term (e.g., X - Y = X - Z), cancel the common term to deduce Y = Z.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When an equation has the same variable subtracted on both sides.
mathgap.example: Failing to cancel X in X - Y = X - Z and treating it as Y = Z.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates a difference to another difference (e.g., 'the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between C and D'), interpret both sides as full signed subtraction expressions and keep the equation as a relation, not as an assignment to a single variable.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a relational statement uses the phrase 'difference between' on either side of an equality.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between C and D' as just C and assigning the left‑hand difference to C alone.

mathgap.description: Treating 'difference between the number of X and Y' as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to interpreting 'difference' as a magnitude, ignoring sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always interpret 'difference between X and Y' as X - Y, preserving order and sign.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements have been processed.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as separate from the main flow and applies them at the end.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately, updating both giver and receiver before processing subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming 'A has N more than B' forces A > B and discarding solutions where A - B is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets 'more' as implying a positive difference.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow the signed difference to be negative; treat the equation algebraically without imposing positivity.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats direct assignments as immutable constants.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as the current value, which can be modified by later transfers.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model reads 'the difference between X and Y' as referring only to X, dropping Y from the equation.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a statement equates a difference to another difference, keep both terms on each side; solve the full equation.
